solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Firstly, dire gut's treated — this treatment may result in issue

definitions.text: this treatment may result in issue

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed and worked over, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient is told that a grim stomach condition is being dealt with first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of gut's stands for 'is' (gut is treated). 'Issue' reads as a problem but is the old word for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Fertility drugs help people conceive, so their result may be offspring, which the law calls issue.

clue.text: Involving Parisian in dogging

parts.note: en is the French word for in
dogging someone is following them closely, tailing them

explanation.surface: Something about a Parisian who gets caught up in following people around.
explanation.definitionFit: If a plan entails something it necessarily involves it, so entailing is a synonym of involving.

clue.text: Pair of heavyweights mostly providing help for US lawman

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight, so a pair of them is ton twice

explanation.surface: Two big boxers are mostly there to back up an American sheriff.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonto is the Native American companion of the Lone Ranger, the masked lawman of US radio and television westerns.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonto is the faithful sidekick who assists the Lone Ranger in the classic western series.

clue.text: Small sum of money former banks turn into cash

indicators.note: banks here means lines the edges of, as banks enclose a river, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman
I QUID, one pound, is a small sum

explanation.surface: A former banker turns a tiny amount of money into cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like a noun about finance but is a verb meaning surrounds. A quid is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate assets is to sell them off and convert them to money.

clue.text: Heads off Tory revolt, and conspiracy to plot

indicators.note: the heads of these words are their opening letters, taken off them

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A party leader heads off a Conservative rebellion and a scheme to plot against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' reads as preventing something, but it asks for the head of each following word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is an area of land, just as a plot is a piece of ground.

clue.text: Jay, say, turns up with jewellery for playing football

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a jay is an example of a bird
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A footballer named Jay arrives wearing showy jewellery for the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Jay looks like a person's name but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Dribbling is moving the ball forward with small kicks, a core skill when playing football.

clue.text: University head's problem departments

parts.note: nits are head lice eggs, a problem in the hair

explanation.surface: A university head's problem with the various departments.
explanation.walkthrough: The head looks like the head of the university, but it is the head on your shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Units are sections of an organisation, as departments are.

clue.text: Deal with reportedly sensitive solicitor

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the sound of these words gives the answer

parts.note: sensitive is SORE and a solicitor of custom is a TOUT, so SORE TOUT, which said aloud runs together

explanation.surface: A touchy lawyer is said to be handling a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is anyone who solicits business, as a ticket tout does.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort out a problem is to handle it and resolve it.

clue.text: Sweat when drained and pant in pain when running

indicators.note: drained of its contents, the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of sweat
to pant for something is to long for it, to itch for it

explanation.surface: A runner sweats and gasps, emptied of energy and aching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweat' and 'pant' read as a runner's exertions, but one is emptied and the other means yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side that comes on during exercise such as running.

clue.text: Giant, metal-covered Tesla's outside

indicators.note: metal-covered means the metal wraps around what follows

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: the word Tesla, the 's being the possessive

explanation.surface: A huge Tesla car is clad in metal on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans were the giant deities of Greek myth, so a titan is a person or thing of great size.

clue.text: Word used to describe heat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in grammar, a word that modifies or describes another
second meaning: a preliminary round of a competition that decides who goes through

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a word for hot weather, but heat is the sporting round.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualifier is both a grammatical modifier and a preliminary race or match.

clue.text: Arab city's tribal politics? Not half!

indicators.note: read with half: not half of the word is kept, so the back half of tribal goes
only half of politics is kept, its back half dropped

explanation.surface: Asking whether an Arab city has tribal politics, with the slang reply 'Not half!' meaning absolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it cuts each of the two words in half.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, an Arab nation, and also a city in Lebanon.

clue.text: British like tucking into Mexican food somewhere in Mexico

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so these letters sit within the food

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican dish
as means like

explanation.surface: Britons enjoy eating Mexican food while somewhere in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' reads as eating, but it means placed inside. The answer also names a hot sauce, a neat red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a state in southeastern Mexico, which gave its name to the sauce.

clue.text: Young heroine and I stop working hard, coming over

indicators.note: coming over means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: A young heroine says she will stop working hard and come over.
explanation.walkthrough: Heidi is the Swiss orphan girl in Johanna Spyri's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Heidi is the child protagonist of the classic children's novel set in the Alps.

clue.text: Bigoted, extremely immoral slur about Gainsborough?

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, taking the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of immoral

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a libel is a damaging slur
Thomas Gainsborough was a founding member of the Royal Academy, an RA

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded critic hurls a vile insult at the painter Gainsborough.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal means intolerant and narrow-minded, close in sense to bigoted.

clue.text: Tech giant almost isn't able to engage current jobseeker

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it on and hold it, so these letters take another inside
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Apple is a giant technology company
can't means isn't able

explanation.surface: A big tech company is almost unable to take on someone looking for work.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the symbol for electric current in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant is a person applying for a post, so a jobseeker.

clue.text: Singers Tom and Johnny getting small kitty

parts.note: Tom Petty was an American rock singer
Johnny Cash was an American country singer

explanation.surface: Two famous singers end up with only a small prize pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty cash is a small fund of money kept for minor office expenses.

clue.text: Film director's against including tear-inducing item

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: anti means against
chopping an onion makes eyes water

explanation.surface: A film director objects to a sad scene that makes audiences cry.
explanation.walkthrough: Michelangelo Antonioni was an Italian film director, maker of Blow-Up.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonioni was a celebrated Italian director of art-house cinema.

clue.text: Merriest time after Welsh footballer eats pork pie

indicators.note: after means this letter comes behind the rest
eats means takes inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: Ryan Giggs is a Welsh footballer
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie

explanation.surface: A happy moment after a Welsh football star tucks into a pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryan Giggs played for Manchester United and Wales. In Cockney rhyming slang a pork pie, often 'porky', is a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Giggliest means most prone to fits of laughter, so the most merry.

clue.text: Unspecific information on e.g. George Orwell

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair, so Eric is his real first name

explanation.surface: Vague facts about an author such as George Orwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general, not particular to one thing.

clue.text: Tech entrepreneur heading for Seychelles after scandal's ending

indicators.note: after puts this letter behind the other piece

parts.note: -gate is the suffix added to scandals after Watergate

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Seychelles

explanation.surface: A tech billionaire flees for the Seychelles once a scandal is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Since Watergate, '-gate' has been tacked onto the names of scandals, so it is a scandal's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft, the archetypal technology entrepreneur.

clue.text: Was a model entertaining underworld fiend?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, as a host holds guests

parts.note: an artist's model sat for the painter
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm

explanation.surface: A question whether a model was keeping company with a criminal monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests gangland, but here it is the classical realm of the dead, Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist delights in cruelty, so is a fiend in the sense of a wicked person.

clue.text: Baked beans go in food container

indicators.note: baked means cooked and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Baked beans are put in a container for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baked beans' reads as one dish, but 'Baked' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a bag of feed hung over a horse's head, a container for food.

clue.text: Furniture stores beginning to invest capital

indicators.note: a thing that stores something keeps it inside

parts.note: a sofa is a piece of furniture

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of invest

explanation.surface: Furniture shops need start-up funds before they can invest capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stores' and 'capital' read as shops and money; one means holds and the other is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: One wears bit of make-up? It may fulfil one's wishes

indicators.note: wears means has on, so this word surrounds the other

parts.note: a gene is a unit of genetic make-up

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a touch of cosmetics, hoping it will make dreams come true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests cosmetics, but it is the genetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie from the lamp grants its master's wishes in folk tales.

clue.text: Had yen or made yen to start with

indicators.note: to start with means this letter goes at the front

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: A trader either longed for Japanese currency or made yen early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The first yen means a longing; the second is the Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a yen for something is to long for it, so had yen means longed.

clue.text: Amount of publicity by Irish politicians

definitions.note: verb: to amount to is to add up to

parts.note: an ad is publicity
the DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party, is a Northern Irish political party

explanation.surface: The quantity of advertising put out by politicians from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amount' reads as a noun but is the verb, as in to amount to a total.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that add up amount to a total; both are phrasal verbs of totting up.

clue.text: Votes from official, prior to promise to keep silent

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is a match official
ere is an old word for before
an NDA, non-disclosure agreement, is a promise of secrecy

explanation.surface: Results of ballots from an official who has signed a promise of secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public ballots on a single question, so they are votes.

clue.text: Rubbish from diva like T Turner or A Franklin

indicators.text: like T Turner or A Franklin
indicators.note: these two singers are written with only an initial for the first name, so the diva's first name is cut to its initial too

parts.note: Diana Ross is a soul diva

explanation.surface: Junk coming from a soul diva such as Tina Turner or Aretha Franklin.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials show the trick: Tina Turner and Aretha Franklin are written as T Turner and A Franklin, so the fellow diva is D Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste matter, the scum on molten metal, so worthless rubbish.

clue.text: Film star has cocaine and crack before brief bit of dialogue

parts.note: charlie is slang for cocaine
to chap is to crack, as skin does in cold

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a line is a single piece of dialogue

explanation.surface: A film star takes cocaine and crack before speaking a few lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests the drug alongside cocaine, but it is the verb for skin splitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the great silent-era screen comedian, famed as the Tramp.
